_note_field: MAINTAINER-ONLY. `note` records why a card is modelled the way it is -- provenance, schema reasoning, what was deliberately not modelled. Never render it in the UI. `caution` is the user-facing field.
_business_note: `business` marks a card issued on business underwriting rather than personal. Absent means personal -- only the field's presence is meaningful, so there is nothing to keep in sync on a hundred and twenty records. It filters the catalogue and nothing else reads it: the ranker does not care whose name is on the account.
_common_note: `common` is a POPULARITY RANK, 1 to 164, and it is EDITORIAL. There is no public card-level ranking of US cardholders -- Nilson publishes issuer volume, not how many people hold a Freedom Unlimited -- so this is judgement, not a sourced fact, and it is the only field here that is. It orders the setup picker so a new user meets mass-market cards first. 21 to 40 were added on 2026-09-27 as the next twenty after the first, 41 to 63 on 2026-09-28 -- store cards, then the remaining tiers of airline and hotel programs already present -- 64 to 82 later that day, the cards of issuers Caddy did not yet cover, 83 to 95 after those, business cards, 96 to 103, smaller store cards, 104 to 110, the missing tiers of covered programs, 111 to 126, Barclays' other co-branded cards, 127 to 140, co-branded business cards, 141 to 151, the business cards of BofA, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Citi, 152, the Kroger card, 153 to 157, the cruise lines' co-branded cards, and 158 to 164, the Atmos and SKYPASS cards, so each batch ranks below the one before by construction. Re-rank it freely; nothing computes from it.
_aliases_note: `aliases` lists the other names one card is sold under, so the setup and Settings searches find it by any of them: the Kroger card is sold as sixteen Kroger banners' cards and shown under Kroger's name only; BofA's pages sell the Atmos cards as Alaska Airlines cards. Search reads it; nothing displays it, and the ranker never reads it.
_only_at_note: `only_at` marks a STORE CARD: the merchant domains where it works, and nowhere else. The ranker drops the card from consideration on any other domain rather than ranking it on its base rate, because recommending a card the till refuses is worse than not mentioning it. base_rate is then what the card adds at that store: where a store pays its free program's members something whatever card they use, that share is left out, because it cannot change which card to use. Store cards with no rewards at all -- Home Depot's, for one -- are deliberately left out: a card that earns nothing can never be the best card to use.
